newsitem.title: USA: GM's GMAC unit Q1 net highest in 10 years.
newsitem.headline: GM's GMAC unit Q1 net highest in 10 years.

text.p: General Motors Acceptance Corp, a wholly owned subsidiary of General Motors Corp, said on Monday its 1997 first quarter consolidated net income rose 20 percent from a year ago to $372 million from $309 million earned in the first quarter of 1996.
Excluding the cumulative effect of a favorable accounting change made in 1991, these results were the highest first-quarter earnings in 10 years, said GMAC President John Rines in a statement.

In the quarter, net income from financing operations, including the GMAC Mortgage Group, totaled $294 million, up eight percent from $272 million earned in the first quarter of 1996. Results for the first three months of 1997 benefited from higher earnings from mortgage operations and increased net interest margins in the United States and Canada.

Motors Insurance Corporation, GMAC's insurance subsidiary, generated net income of $78 million in the first quarter, compared with $37 million earned last year. The earnings increase was principally due to higher capital gains, the company said.
